title: Detecting Weather Fronts from Satellite Observations: What Does Reanalysis Add?
abstract: arXiv:2611.08148v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Weather fronts are transition regions between air masses with contrasting thermodynamic properties and are associated with mid-latitude precipitation and severe weather. We investigate machine learning (ML) methods for detecting weather fronts and quantify the contribution of reanalysis data to performance. We compare two configurations of the same ML model for pixel-wise frontal classification over the North Atlantic and Europe: (1) using only geostationary infrared satellite observations, and (2) additionally using 28 ERA5 reanalysis fields. The satellite-only model achieves a neighbourhood critical success index at a 150 km tolerance (CSI@150) of $0.402$, which lies within the range of agreement between analyses from different meteorological services. translated_title: 从卫星观测中检测天气锋面：再分析数据能带来什么增益？

tldr: 该研究比较了仅用静止红外卫星观测与额外加入ERA5再分析数据的机器学习天气锋面检测模型，发现再分析数据可将检测性能显著提升（CSI@150从0.402提高至0.575），其中低层风场是仅靠卫星数据最难预测的信息。
en_tdlr: This study shows that adding ERA5 reanalysis fields to a machine learning weather front detection model using only geostationary infrared satellite observations substantially improves performance (CSI@150 rising from 0.402 to 0.575), with low-level winds being the least predictable from satellite data alone.
